title: Detecting Direct Left Recursion in Grammar Dictionaries
description: Scan grammar dictionaries to find nonterminals whose productions start with themselves, and compare left-recursive and right-recursive arithmetic grammars.
source: draft: agy free model + edit: codex

steps.description: `find_left_recursive(grammar)` loops over `(head, productions)` in `grammar.items()` and checks each production `rhs`. When `rhs` is non-empty and `rhs[0] == head` (line 9), line 10 adds `head` to `left_recursive`.
`report(name, grammar)` calls `find_left_recursive(grammar)` and prints either the sorted list of directly left-recursive nonterminals or `no direct left recursion found`.

Lines 25-43 define three grammar dictionaries. `grammar_lr` uses `E -> E + T | T` and `T -> T * F | F`. The right-recursive rewrite `grammar_rr` uses `E -> T E'` and `E' -> + T E' | []`; `grammar_bp` uses `S -> ( S S ) | []`.

Compare lines 26-27 (`grammar_lr`) with lines 33-36 (`grammar_rr`). In `grammar_lr`, `rhs[0]` of `["E", "+", "T"]` and `["T", "*", "F"]` matches `head`. In `grammar_rr`, the self-calls `"E'"` and `"T'"` sit at the end of `rhs` after `"+"` or `"*"`.

steps.question: When lines 45-47 run `report` on `grammar_lr`, `grammar_rr`, and `grammar_bp`, what does `find_left_recursive` return for each?
steps.answer: It returns `{'E', 'T'}` for `grammar_lr` (`LEFT-RECURSIVE nonterminals = ['E', 'T']`) and an empty set (`no direct left recursion found`) for both `grammar_rr` and `grammar_bp`.

steps.description: Lines 45-47 call `report` on all three grammars and print the results.
At trace step 21 inside `find_left_recursive(grammar_lr)`, `rhs` is `['E', '+', 'T']` and `rhs[0] == 'E'`, so line 10 adds `'E'` to `left_recursive`.
